7571.info_text: One of the few known locations in Germany with any arcade games. / Due to gambling laws, until 2003 video games were classified the same as gambling machines, only available to those over the age of 18. Gambling casinos did get the occasional game, but they are not allowed to advertise in the paper or on the net. Therefore machine locations were only available via word of mouth. / Now it is easier to get a license to have traditional video games, but the law was reversed so late in the day. Arcades were already in decline so no point to open new ones. / This place can be found directly via a subway exit from the main station.

10739.info_text: To get to Lotte World find your way to Jamsil Station on Line 2 or 8. Follow the many signs to the park. Admission is cheaper with a Shinhan bank card. / Lotte World is a huge Korean theme park, perhaps the best. It is a knock off of the Disney Parks but it is pretty cool on its own merit. It is the world's largest indoor theme park (and it is indeed impressive). There are a ton of good rides here, Atlantis Adventure, Cosmic Express, Pharoah's Fury and Gyro Swing were my favorites. / The arcade locations are all located in the indoor park. The is one arcade, the Moroccan arcade, with a lot of fighting games (Tekken 6 etc.) The arcade with rhythm games was located next to the "Happy Tree Picnic" ride, and "Marion Crepes". It is on the first floor. There is another arcade on floor three by the big loop of "French Revolution" with nothing of interest. There is one more arcade connected to the Folk Museum apparently, but I did not have a chance to explore. / Overall it's a great park, I expected a lot more rhythm games though. Maybe they are hidden somewhere...

10801.info_text: Associació A.R.C.A.D.E. (aka ARCADE.cat) is a non-profit cultural association aiming the preservation and divulgation of arcade games and culture, by a wide array of means: collaborating with cultural entities and other media such as films, podcasts, radios, etc, organizing tournaments, and restoring machines of its private collection. Our main objective is to preserve the feel and essence of old arcades, as well as modern ones. / The association is run collaboratively by its members in their free time as a labor of love, with frequent events, workshops and tournaments. Its premises is home to an extensive collaborative collection of arcade and pinball machines that cover over 40+ years of arcade history. It has a mix of dedicated cabinets (rhythm games, racing games, classic games, etc.) as well as Candy cabinets and Spanish generic cabinets from the 90s, with games usually being switched from time to time. All of them are set on Free To Play. / Keep in mind, this is not a game center open to the public. Access to the premises is for members and accompanying guests only. However, we hold many different tournaments throughout the year (A.R.C., SHMUPFEST, TBAP and more upcoming)...

10808.info_text: La industria de los videojuegos diseñados para salones recreativos, dejó de estar presente en Europa a finales del año 2000. Los videojuegos domésticos de nueva generación, los impuestos abusivos, y la crisis hizo que las maquinas recreativas dejaran de fabricarse, y lo más grave… que estos sistemas fueran destruidos para no pagar las tasas mensuales que sus propietarios debían abonar sólo por tenerlas. / En Arcade Planet, hemos conseguido rescatar y restaurar las mejores recreativas de la historia, y preservando los mejores juegos de todos los sistemas. / Arcade Planet ofrece su increíble colección de Arcades para eventos, exposiciones, organización de torneos, y sesiones de juego libre “free play”. / Con esta iniciativa aquellos que jugaron en los 80 y 90 volverán a recordar los mejores ratos de ocio de sus vidas… y las nuevas generaciones descubrirán la especial interpretación del modo de juego creado para salones recreativos… donde el único propósito es la diversión inmediata. / (PLEASE CHECK OPENING TIMES ON EITHER FACEBOOK OR INSTAGRAM, BETWEEN 15:00 AND 17:00 THERE'S A PAUSE AND THE ARCADE CLOSES THOSE 2 HOURS). / The out of order board was the same as Litwak’s Arcade. No...

10809.info_text: At Arcade Rebirth, our goal is to preserve and share arcade culture through an experience that aims to rival authentic Japanese arcades. / To play, to connect, to unwind—our space brings together rhythm games and classic arcade machines, all carefully maintained to recreate the magic of traditional game centers. / To offer a safe and inclusive environment is just as important to us as the games themselves. We want everyone to feel welcome, whether you're here to discover, compete, or just enjoy. / To visit, simply book your spot through our website. We open Thursday to Sunday, including public holidays.

10865.info_text: Nextage is a non-profit association in Madrid and the meeting point for the largest rhythm game communities in Spain. This is where fans of Pump It Up (PIU), ITG, DDR, Sound Voltex, and Beatmania IIDX live, with tournaments, challenges, and meetups in a close, authentic environment. We're not a business: we're a community built by and for arcade lovers. If you're looking to improve, enjoy, or simply share this hobby with people like you, this is your place. / Access to the warehouse is for members and accompanying guests. You can also appoint a visit on the open days at weekends on their website. / Entrance fee is 7€ (or 10€ for both weekend days), and you can become a member for 30€/month, which includes entry into a private group, and being able to come on weekdays / If you'd like more information on the project or would like to arrange for a visit, please contact at our social media.

In our clean and safe environment, where families can spend quality time together, children can enjoy playing alongside their parents, while adults can relax with a cup of tea or coffee. / Fantasyland Game Center is open every day from 12:00 PM to 8:00 PM.

11182.info_text: The only maintained & publicly accessible PiU cabinet in İstanbul resides in this arcade. It was restored by Funlab Staff with the help of TRPIU community member bluein recently and reopened for use. Currently Funlab is on the lookout for any newer data. Contact the number in Turkish or @BlueinRedout on X (Formerly Twitter) for business inquiries regarding this cab. / Once you exit Kocatepe Metro station, take a right and enter Forum İstanbul. Go up to the foodcourt. The arcade will be in front of you next to the Joylab UFO Catcher machines.

11221.info_text: Welcome to / Ace of Lanes / We are a firm believer that time isn't the main thing, it's the only thing and that time flies, but memories last forever. Ace of Lanes in Bishops Stortford has been truly inspired by being a venue to build unforgettable memories. / With that in mind, we felt adding the steampunk touch would be the only way to go. The essence of Steampunk within great books such as Around the World in Eighty Days, The Steam House, 20,000 Leagues Under the Sea and The Time Machine. Their elements of time travel, mad science, combining the natural with the mechanical, we felt it would be the ultimate theme would be so true for Ace of Lanes.

11222.info_text: Very small arcade out the back for pub customers. Includes a Euromix cabinet with a Euromix 2 sign.

machine_prices.ddr: 50p for three songs, and doubles but needs to be double checked

11229.info_text: Blackpool Arcade club brings the classics back to Blackpool whilst also offering modern gaming all for one inclusive price. Featuring classics including Pac Man, Space Invaders, Outrun, Time Crisis and all your favourite games from the 80s and 90s, plus modern classics such as House of the Dead 5, Luigi's Mansion, Air Hockey Basketball and Pinball. / Arcade is next to Blackpool F.C. stadium / Once inside all games are free to play!

11230.info_text: Pay to Enter arcade situated within an industrial complex within Bury situated over four separate floors. Plenty of parking outside. / Floor 0 / Ground Floor : Mix of cabs including DDR A3, StepManiaX, Dancing Stage, the 16+ pinball room, and other games. / Floor 1: DanceRush Stardom, Sports Cabs (Basketball, Skeeball, Airhockey), Modern Consoles (Xbox, Switch) and large co-op cabinets typically found in UK arcades (Mission Impossible, House of the Dead, Luigi's Mansion). / Floor 2: Japanese import rhythm games live here like SDVX, Museca, Nostalgia, Wacca, Chunithm, maimai, Taiko, GITADORA etc. along with Astro/Blast City cabs, racing games, and some PC setups. / Floor 3: Retro arcade cabs, and the dining area with food served and a party room. / All floors have bar areas where (quite reasonably priced) drinks (both soft and alcoholic) can be purchased. You can purchase hot food like pizza, burgers, nachos and more at the bar on Floor 3, with plenty of seating. Uses a restaurant pager system for food orders, so you can keep walking around while you wait. Bag storage lockers are located at reception, just ask security to access it. / Entry Prices: / £18.00 - Adult entry / £10.00...

11231.info_text: Pay to enter, free to play arcade. / Adult (16+): £18 / Child (5-15): £10 / Family (2 adults, 2 children): £46 / Under 5: Free / Opening hours are extended on school & summer holidays. / Monthly Unlimited Passes can be bought online or at the counter which allow unlimited entry to the arcade. / 1 Month - (16+): £49.00 (5-15): £23.00 / 2 Months - (16+): £79 (5-15): £39.50 / 3 Months - (16+): £99.00 (5-15): £49.50 / Second venue after Arcade Club Bury. / E-Amusement passes can be bought at the counter for £10. / E-Amusement Games are connected to a private network (https://projectflower.eu), scores will not be visible on KONAMI's site. / Parking is free for guests. Additional parking is available in Morrisons' car park, opposite the venue. Morrisons' car park closes at 10pm, beware if you are leaving afterwards. / Staff are very friendly and know their stuff, don't hesitate to talk to them if a machine is messing up. / Friday is adults only after 6pm.

11233.info_text: Multiple "coin" pricing options, though they'll give you a token card for each of the machines there. Buy these at the bar / £10 > 20 coins = £3 per credit / £20 > 45 coins = £2.67 per credit / £50 > 120 coins = £2.50 per credit / £100 > 260 coins = ~£2.31 per credit / £200 > 600 coins = £2 per credit / (Cost per credit assuming 6 coin cost) / Google also seems to list that they are open from 12am - 3:30am daily as well as the other 12pm-10pm listed opening times

11234.info_text: Freeplay arcade as part of the Cains brewery venue group. 3 floors alongside a newer 'Level 4' extension to the middle floor. Ground floor contains mostly spectacle/redemption games like World's Largest PAC-MAN and Super Bikes 3, top floor contains mostly modern consoles and PCs. Middle floor is the largest and has most of the authentic cabs, and the extension has most of the rarer imports - card-compatible games listed on the site are all networked. / Canteen is open on weekends - kids allowed until 9PM Mon-Thurs, or 6PM Fri-Sun. Open 7 days a week, with parking on the side of the building.

11235.info_text: Astro City is located on the second floor overlooking the High Street and Southchurch Road. After you get to the top of the stairs, you'll enter a small room with a number of arcade machines. Go through the door on the left to the end of the corridor and you'll find the main arcade area. Continue to the left, past the snack bar and you'll arrive at the new food area. / PUBLIC OPENING / Public opening is now restricted to various two and three hour sessions throughout the week. There's a complete list of session times on our website, just click on "Free Play Sessions" on the drop down. As of 19/12/18 there are 56 machines and games set to free play and entry is only £5 per person. / PRIVATE PARTIES / All other times are reserved for private children's birthday parties and adult arcade hire. / FACILITIES / Toilets, snack/coffee bar and a food eating area. / OTHER MACHINES / Astro City has a large number of machines, games and rides that do not feature in the main list. So not wanting to leave any machines out, here's a supplementary list. / Whappa Snappa, / Crab Panic, / Air Hockey, / Speedball, / Feeding Time, / Squid Spies, / Hammer, / 2 x Boxers, / Taz Ride, / Bear Ride, / Bask...

11256.info_text: Open until 10pm everyday again, but they'll still close early nowadays if really quiet. / Try to remember something to brush the pads off with, as often are pretty sandy, though a bit better since the ddr moved to the other side of the arcade. Ddr has contactless card pay system / b]Note: Gets extremely busy during summer holidays and school breaks.[/b] The wait for DDR isn't usually longer than one or two, though. If you have not played this, remember as soon as you select your style and after the caution, you can play the tutorial if you wish (unless of course you're playing Doubles, where after the caution you go straight to song selection). / Quite a good arcade, a good mixture of new games and classics. The majority of the machines are located around the edges of the arcade. Typical price per credit is £1 but some games take contactless payments by card, it's an arcade on a beach so there's a lot of other stuff to do, there's shops literally a couple of steps away from the arcade's entrance, the atmosphere is really good and if you play DDR you may get a crowd!

11372.info_text: Just opened, located within the mall

11374.info_text: Located within Folly Farm (paid entry) there is some arcade cabs located near the adventure playground section indoors / Previously a DDR euromix with wide-screen mod was here however removed around 2020 :( / Now seems to be mainly small crane games and such

11375.info_text: Games are set to Free Play, with a £5 entry fee.

machine_prices.ddr: 2x quarter dollar coins - 1 song only. / Non-stop mode enabled! You can play 4 songs in a row for 2x quarter dollar coins.

11376.info_text: Our Elephant and Castle arcade bar opened in August 2021 as one of the original businesses launching the new development of Elephant Park. We have over 20 original arcade and pinball machines, 2 big-screen gaming setups, and 4 inside and 4 outside console booths! All of these are original machines, restored by our in-house team, with an extensive list of nostalgic retro games. Goldeneye 007, anyone? / The booths can be pre booked, or booked at the bar if they are available. / November 2025: all games are 2 USD quarters (2 x 25 cents). You can buy 4 quarters for £2.5, or 18 quarters for £10.

11377.info_text: "AT ALL OUR VENUES, UNDER 18S ARE ONLY ALLOWED IF ACCOMPANIED BY A RESPONSIBLE ADULT. OUR VENUES ARE OVER 18S ONLY AFTER 19:00." [i][ From the [url=https://fourquarters.bar/faqs/]FAQ[/url] on their website, retrieved 5Feb23 ][/i] / All games added are as listed on the website. / 4 quarters are £2.50. Games cost 1-2 usually.

11378.info_text: They've got vintage arcade machines, classic console booths, pinball and a stunning selection of cocktails and craft beers. / Vintage arcade cabinets, craft beers, amazing cocktails and great vibes. / They've got classic Nintendo, Sega and PlayStation booths too.

11379.info_text: It's time. / £10 weekdays. £15 weekends. / Aime Cards: £7 / e-amusement Cards: £7 / NESiCA: £7 / BANAPASSPORT: £7 / Gloves: £1 / Premium Gloves: £3 / Phone tripods are available near the dance games, lots of the other cabs have phone holders / X (twitter): @FreeplayC

11381.info_text: Mainly ticket redemption games and waterfall/pushers. Has a few arcade games as well, including an X2, which has been moved from Llandudno Pier to here

11382.info_text: Another Fun Factory, arcade cards from the other Fun Factory can be used here, general redemption and such games

11383.info_text: General claw machines, coin games, racing games, etc. / The downstairs is completely closed and used for storage now

11384.info_text: Planning a visit? Be sure to check the opening dates and hours as the location may be closed when out of season. / Opening dates: / http://www.pleasure-beach.co.uk/uploads/PICS/opening-dates.jpg / Opening hours: / http://www.pleasure-beach.co.uk/uploads/DOCS/daily-opening-hours.pdf

11385.info_text: Located on the second floor. Fun Station has games and dodgems while Prize Station is mostly redemption.

11386.info_text: This is a small looking arcade that is actually relatively large. There's a mix of modern games as well as some older coin droppper/ pusher games.

11388.info_text: Two floors - downstairs features prize redemption/gambling/newer video game cabinets up against the back wall, as of 2022 upstairs has now been refurbished to become "Retro Zone" with a selection of older videos + pinballs, as well as further redemption. / Owners also manage the neighbouring Fun City; smaller venue and no video titles.

machine_prices.iidx: 100P / Standard Start / 130P / Premium Start / 204P / Premium Free 10 minutes / 278P / Premium Free 15 minutes / 352P / Premium Free 20 minutes / 6.2 Funcoins / Standard Start
machine_prices.sdvx: 100P / LIGHT START / 130P / STANDARD START / 200P / PREMIUM TIME / 5.7 Funcoins / LIGHT START

11389.info_text: Small venue in the shopping centre with two floors. Upstairs has mostly redemption games as well as multiple pinball machines, two DDR white cabs running DDR A20 PLUS and the brand new Universal cabinet running DDR World. The downstairs basement area has a selection of BEMANI games including beatmania IIDX, SOUND VOLTEX, REFLEC BEAT, jubeat, pop'n music and DanceDanceRevolution. Ask at the desk to access downstairs. / Almost all BEMANI games support video recording, where the last 5 minutes of gameplay can be saved and downloaded over the Wi-Fi network. More details can be found by scanning the QR code from any supported cabinet. / All games here use a card system with points called Funcoins. They will take card payments only and the following denominations get you coins with extra bonuses from £15-£25: / £5 - 25 coins / £10 - 50 coins / £15 - 100 coins / £20 - 125 coins / £25 - 200 coins / £50 - 425 coins / PASELI can also be purchased with cash only from the prize counter at a rate of 1:100 in £10, and £20 packs (for example, £10 will get you 1000 PASELI). The machines downstairs are on an e-amusement server emulator known as Ganymede. Cards are available for purchase at the f...

11391.info_text: June '23- a surprisingly nice arcade for a funfair that looks quite dilapidated when you first drive past. No DDR anymore, but 5 good pinballs. The 2nd arcade appears to now be Lazer tag or somat, and has a kids soft area beyond the inside diner. Some interesting ticket prizes compared to other places, and many older 2p pushers/waterfalls that are actually easily winnable compared to all the newest ones for anyone into that. Signs say arcade open year round. / Funland has two arcades, which ill label as the main arcade and the cafe arcade. / The main arcade has an ITG but was not turned on. Also has a large number of other games including some pinball machines. / The cafe arcade has a euromix 2 which is in decent condition and some older games.

11392.info_text: Seasonal, largish arcade, next to another seasonal largish one. On a little road in between the caravan parks

11394.info_text: Small arcade with 2p coin pushers, a small selection of arcade games and pool upstairs

machine_prices.ddr: 4 tokens STANDARD MODE / 40 tokens is £10, discounts at higher token charges

11395.info_text: Arcade is on top most floor of shopping centre, requires a card swiping systems for the machines / Credits are loaded up onto the card at either a dedicated machine or at the counter / Both cash and card are okay

11396.info_text: Mostly just ticket games / Uses a card payment system, £5 gives you 20 credits, discounts are only applied after you top up £20

11397.info_text: Funstation Leeds, The Light. / Uses a card swipe system with tokens. £1 gets you 4 Tokens. When buying larger bundles you can get extra tokens.

11398.info_text: Venue is on the ground floor of the Xscape building just behind the escalators. / Games use swipe cards. Top-up kiosks accept card or cash. / Parking is 80p an hour (blue bays) or 50p an hour (pink bays). Free parking after 6pm.

11399.info_text: In the Cornerhouse centre. As with all Funstations, it's card-based, most of the games are ticket redemption, but there are some arcades in there. Videos are around the 4-5 credit range. No free Wi-Fi here or nearby so you'll have to use mobile data to scan game QR codes. / StepManiaX cab doing most of the heavy lifting here, if it's a loc test and eventually disappears it's going to be so much more difficult to recommend this place tbh / [4, Sep '24 - It's been about two years so I RECKON it's a keeper, lol. From the sounds of it, it's one of the big money-spinners, so there's no reason for it to go away...hopefully.] / Token Prices: / £1 = 4 Tokens / £5 = 20 Tokens / £10 = 40 Tokens / £15 = 80 Tokens / £25 = 140 Tokens / £55 = 320 Tokens

11400.info_text: Redemption Arcade and Hologate VR. / Same spot as the old Namco Wonderpark (RIP). Don't expect frequent location tests of games from Japan here this time though / This arcade uses a card system to save tokens and earned tickets. / 1 token = 25p

11401.info_text: Redemption arcade inside the Xscape building. This arcade uses a card system. Cards can be bought at the counter or at numerous self service kiosks around the arcade. 1 token seems to be worth £0.25. Buying more than £15 at once will get you better value.

11402.info_text: Inside the main building on the left, has burger king merged with it (for some reason lol) / Inside / arcade is closed during winter time / Caravan park arcades are in same area, in middle of park. Accessible to non-residents and a large parking area by arcade/entertainment area. Arcades get really hot if warm/sunny. / 1st StepManiaX in Wales!

11403.info_text: Broken Euromix 1, Euromix 2 in good condition if a little quiet.

11404.info_text: Located inside Kiln Park, you do need a entertainment pass to enter the building (if they are checking lol) so this isn't available if just visiting and only to guests at the caravan park - still added just in case anyone is there lol / Typical caravan park arcade with 2p machines and general redemption and such

11405.info_text: This info is as of 29th July 2011. / There are two DS EM1 machines - one of them has a EM2 sign on it. Don't be fooled! The downstairs one has mega-loud bass and is 4 songs a go. They are both reasonably loud - in fact the downstairs one can be heard from outside! However, the pads aren't very good, which is what can be expected. They have gotten considerably worse however, and the staff have so far refused to fix them because "technically, they still work". I have managed to pass the hardest songs on them though and some people I have seen have even FC'd (albeit on basic). And of course, if you play anything above a 5 foot then you get a big crowd! / There's also a Guitar Hero. I'm rubbish at Guitar Hero so I didn't play it, but it seemed to work well from what I saw watching other people play it. / The overall quality of the machines is mediocre. Every machine is slowly dying, and the staff seem not to care. They still have the machines on so they take your money, and only then do you discover that the machine is broken.

11406.info_text: Arcade in Lakeside, Haven. Mostly redemption games

11408.info_text: Large arcade, split into multiple businesses. Town has a number of arcades, but this is the only one with a DDR. It has a bowling alley as well as a café, small kiddy go karts and a soft play. Looks to be open year round. Used to have 2 Euromix 2 cabs, but now has neither and has been replaced with a Euromix 1 cab in very poor condition.

11409.info_text: Multi-Activity Venue opened 13/12/2023. There's a small arcade here along with bowling, mini-golf and other various games. Food also served as well. / Opening hours over school holidays are extended as follows: / Monday - Thursday 11:30 - 21:00 / Friday - Sunday 11:30 - 22:00

11410.info_text: VR/Retro/Rhythm gaming arcade. / Has minibar with drinks and snacks. / Physical tokens for the cabinets can be withdrawn at the machine to the right of the front desk. / £5 - 5 Tokens / £10 - 12 Tokens / £20 - 25 Tokens

11411.info_text: Closed for extensive refurbishment. / Preston has a brand new entertainment venue. Think Gravity MAX, but big.

11412.info_text: No rhythm games. Claw Machines and some Arcade 1UP cabs

11414.info_text: Store consisting of only gashapon machines. Arcade section removed.

machine_prices.ddr: 3 songs for £2 / Singles / 3 songs for £4 / Doubles

11416.info_text: This arcade has three floors. The ground floor has some games on the left hand side. The second floor has a mixture of games and both the DDR's. The third floor has toilets. / Update 25/08/2019 / Some games have been removed (HOTD3/Elvis Pinball) and others are in pretty poor condition. DDR X is decent but avoid the Euromix. / Update 05/11/2022 / I was there in just the Summer and I can confirm they no longer have the Euromix or the DDR X. They do however still have the DDR A20 Plus as well as the Guitar Hero Arcade, but if you're desperate to get some more DDR action there is an X2 just up the road.

11417.info_text: Not many games here in this arcade, considering it is a public area.

11418.info_text: nice looking bowling place with a small arcade

11419.info_text: A small barcade in portsmouth that has a small selection of games and also karaoke and darts / 18+ only (they said they might open it up to families with kids on sundays but they are unsure) / not to far of a walk from clarence pier if you want to play some other games too / Pricing: / Monday - Friday £10/1 hour / Weekend £15/1 hour / if its not too busy that arent too strict on the hour / if you want to see their current games please refer to the list here as their socials take pictures at other arcades to promote games they dont have

11420.info_text: Next to/part of beefcakes and shakes. Doesn’t show up on google maps as of 22/3/25

11421.info_text: Seaside arcade situated on the Marine Parade on the Yarmouth Seafront. / A fairly big complex that got expanded into where Yesterday's World was in 2016. Includes redemption/ticket machines, videos games, a gambling area, pushers and of course the ITG machine. It's gone through quite a few changes in its lifetime but is still very well taken care of and is worth a play if you're in the area. / StepManiaX DX installed March 2024! / - Nearest public toilet: opposite the arcade in the Marina Centre / - Nearest ATM: in the arcade the ATM charges £1.50 for withdrawals. The nearest free ATM is in town, around a 10 minute walk. / - Closing times: the arcade usually closes at 10PM, but at peak times during the easter/summer it stays open later.

11422.info_text: At the Golden Coast Leasure Park, you don't need to be staying to visit but recommended. / Bowling and table tennis downstairs

11423.info_text: UPDATE: 13/06/2022 / Now has StepmaniaX which replaces the SN cab that was here previously which is now at games wharf nearby. / The right section is open throughout the year, the left side is only open on weekends and weekdays from March-October. This section can be open on some Fridays during winter months. / Opening times listed are for summer months. / Usually gets some new cabs in each year around March till June.

11426.info_text: Very impressive DDRX2* machine overall, however 2P left arrow has a mild tendency to stick now and again. / Trivia: Golden Palms used to have a thriving Bemani scene, with Team Paranoia from Dancegames.com using it as their local. There was a DDR 1.5, Pump Prex and Beatmania until 2003/4.

11427.info_text: Caravan park arcade, on main road and open to non-residents / (Closed during the COVID-19 outbreak)

11429.info_text: Quote from Facebook: / "We cater to families looking for fun and prizes in our Family Entertainment Centre, as well as offering an Adult Gaming Centre, with the very latest machines" / NOTE: Facebook and google searches seem to claim its open 24 hours

11430.info_text: Fun and wacky, adult only, crazy golf venue with a bar. / Also has karaoke and an arcade / The arcade machines generally accept money or tokens, however I don't know the token rates / amounts for the money

11431.info_text: [18+] / Whilst the golf requires booking, you can visit just for the arcade. / At the door (with ID check) they usually ask if you have a booking, just say your here just for arcade and u can go in / Japanese style decor similar to Gravity Max Wandsworth, and hip bar and food area. Pretty cool mini golf too. DDR volume is very low compared to music throughout the venue so good luck.

11432.info_text: Only open on Saturdays and Sundays outside of summer. / Under the Arches, Graham runs the last independent arcade in Brighton. / There is a converted Euromix 2 with a flat screen. It lags, but the pads are good. / Easily the best pads in Brighton. / After a flood, the old games went, but there is a MAME cabinet with about 20 SF II variations on it, plus the Alpha and Xmen Vs Streetfighter series. The cab itself has a very clunky button setup, but in good condition. / Check my video! / http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ERPiBcMy2jA

11434.info_text: ⚠ Access to the pier (and therefore arcade) costs £2. / Closing times vary depending on the weather and pier attendance. / Click for a older pier tour by Toby. / http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kdg2T8bmCOM

11436.info_text: An arcade inside Bluewater Shopping Centre in the Upper Rose Gallery. It uses a top-up Player Card and app instead of coins.

11437.info_text: An arcade which is technically named Fun Box. / Utilizes a top-up card system for payment and ticket collection. £1 per 10 tokens, with bulk discounts beginning at £25.

11438.info_text: An arcade which is technically named Fun Box, located on the second floor of Gravity, which is accessible via the Southside Shopping Center until 7pm; after which the entrance and exit is on the opposite end of the building, off Garratt Lane. / A good place for a random gaming outing. Go-kart circuit, redemption and arcade floor, mini golf, bowling, VR, AR, E-gaming room. / Japanese styling in most of it, a few bars, and an alright food offering. Many pinball machines and a few cabs hosting retro titles. Pretty cool place to hang. / Utilizes a top-up card system for payment and ticket collection. £1 per 10 tokens, with bulk discounts beginning at £25.

11442.info_text: This bowling alley has a large arcade with a lot of very nice condition games. As well as being in good condition, there is quite a few that you don't usually see around as much! / This used to be called Starbowl however was closed and taken over by Lane 7, who have completely turned it around. Before the take over it was pretty much a wasteland, so it's great that they've made it such a lively place. / Edit 02/08/2023: / The arcade has switched to a card system, with a Bay Tek redemption machine for prizes. The cards have the Level X logo because it's the other half of Lane 7 and I'm sure they'll change the name at some point to match the other locations. / Games not listed on this website@ / Magic Arrow 5.7 Tokens / Shoot It Win It 5.7 Tokens / Wheel of Fortune (Ice) 6.8 Tokens / Skill Cut 5.7 Tokens / Super Kixx Pro 6.8 Tokens / Hoops FX 8 Tokens

11443.info_text: Newly opened Bowling and Arcade centre located on the Ground Floor. / Easy access to Shopping Centre Entrance as Tram stops right outside. / Home to Scotland’s first DDR WORLD Universal Model. / Lane7 and Level X cards and credits can be used at this venue. / Prices and more games will be added in the coming weeks.

11444.info_text: Bowling alley with other activities such as darts, shuffle board and an arcade / Arcade uses a card credit system: / £10 = 60 credits / £20 = 130 credits / £30 = 200 credits / £50 = 350 credits

11445.info_text: Very small amount of games spread across 4 different arcades. / The highlight is daytona championship USA, the rest is just ticket games. / There's also a VR area which has 3 HTC vives at £7 for 20 minutes. Games include beat saber among others

11446.info_text: Only seaside arcade I know of in Southend that is not owned by Star Amusements. Tightly compact place stuffed to the brim with some great games both old and new, joint to "Hamilton's Ice Cream Parlour". / Some of the nicest, chattiest staff of an arcade I've ever spoken with!

11448.info_text: A little arcade tucked away on the promenade. Note that it's mainly locked up during winter months, but it's sometimes open for school holidays, etc. / Notable for having a JP DDRMAX2 cabinet in immaculate condition, although unfortunately it's supposedly running EuroMix2 (but was broken when I last saw it).

11451.info_text: Free to enter quite small amusement park with an arcade. Closing times differ depending on the time of year. / From the website: / January-May closes at 6pm / Easter Holidays closes at 8pm / May Half Term closes at 8pm / June closes at 7pm / July closes at 8pm / Summer Holidays closes at 9pm / September closes at 7pm / October-December closes at 6pm

11453.info_text: 02/12/2015 / Still broken and not working / [b]Update:[/b] 11/09/2011 / The EuroMIX2 machine is broken and is awaiting a new 32mb flash card. Pads and monitor are in great shape. / 23/10/2011 / Now working

11454.info_text: A few redemption games here, for people who booked only.

11456.info_text: Loads of redemption, plus a few games.

11457.info_text: Arcade as part of the Golden Sands Holiday Park in Haven. / Contains many redemption games, simulators, video games, kiddie rides, and pushers. / Now has a StepManiaX Deluxe Cabinet which is online and running the latest update. / The arcade runs on either coins or tokens used to play certain machines.

11458.info_text: Redemption heavy arcade with very few video arcade games, a large amount of VR simulators, slot machines, and kids rides.

11459.info_text: This was originally the Richardsons Holiday Centre, but has now transferred to Haven. / The arcade here is operated by Playnation by Inspired. / Most machines here were carried over from the previous owners, but this will likely change in the future.

11460.info_text: Not your usual holiday park, it's filled with redemption.

11461.info_text: Mainly ticket games, mainly opearetd by Playnation.

11462.info_text: Holiday park arcade ran by Namco with the Namco funscape branding. / Uses cards which you top up with money similar to Sega Prize zone / Caravan ownership or rental proof is required to enter the park.

11464.info_text: Had some really old games here, this was from a year or so ago so may not still be here but thought it was worth adding

11465.info_text: Is along the promenade from Coney Island amusement park, adjacent to Hi Tide pub and restaurant. / Very large and well kept arcade. A lot of redemption games. / Supernova is still upstairs with the bowling

11467.info_text: Paid entry freeplay arcade, £13 for a 90 min slot (subject to change, still on opening week fees) / Booking in advance mandatory / All games on rotation with other venues, game lineup may change periodically / what3words: beats.orange.crunch / Opening times differ on school holidays: / Mon-Sat (school hols): 10:00-20:00 / Sun (school hols): 10:00-18:30 / Early closure all days if no sessions are booked, no walkins afaik

11468.info_text: Free play arcade with a rotating selection of games / usually open on weekends unless there is school holidays in which they are open all week / Pricing: / General Admission - £12.50/h - if you have a disability your carer can enter free of charge with your ticket / 4 Person family ticket - £40/h - Must be at least 1 adult (18+) and 2 children / All games are on freeplay after entry / Important note: / the venue will close at 18:30 if there are no bookings made for the final 19:00 session. / 18:00 on Sunday if there are no bookings made for the 17:30 session.

11469.info_text: All machines are set on free play. £11.95 entry fee for an hour of gameplay.

11470.info_text: High Score is a arcade in Newbury opened December 2020. All machines are set to free play and there is a face mask requirement.

11472.info_text: Free play arcade with a rotating selection of games / usually open on weekends unless there is school holidays in which they are open all week / Pricing: / General Admission - £12.50/h - if you have a disability your carer can enter free of charge with your ticket / 4 Person family ticket - £40/h - Must be at least 1 adult (18+) and 2 children / All games are on freeplay after entry / Important note: / the venue will close at 18:30 if there are no bookings made for the final 19:00 session. / 18:00 on Sunday if there are no bookings made for the 17:30 session.

11473.info_text: Pay to enter, 5th branch of High Score / Seems to do only hour long sessions for about £11 / School hols open til 8pm everyday / Rest of year Fri-Sun

11474.info_text: new arcade, but only has guitar hero and ddr x2 for rhythm games, theres a bunch of racing games but ill need to look into that. £12.50 per hour.

11475.info_text: -Driving simulators / -Arcade games / -Music Arcade games (e.g. ddr)(doesn't know if it is still there btw) / -Air hockey / -Change machine / Not sure on the details (will update when found out) / 10am - 6pm (school holidays)

11476.info_text: Small collection of MAME cabinets and pinball tables.

11477.info_text: 2 floor beach side small arcade / The only arcade I am aware of in Filey

11480.info_text: No DDR but probably better selection of games than most Hollywood Bowl locations if you're into shooters + racing games.

11481.info_text: Had DDR for many years before the machine was removed. Arcade is mostly ticket redemption machines but there are a few newer games. Was at one point between the late '00s and early 2010's a Sega active zone, if memory and obscure tweets serve me right.

11483.info_text: EuroMIX 2 gone as of 29/03/2019 / The first machine in this place was EZ2 Dancer. The owner had a good knowledge of arcades and also imported Beatmania. The subsequent owners had no idea, and scrapped both cabinets. Eventually a DDR Euromix was installed in late 2001. This was upgraded to Euromix 2, and has been there ever since. No maintenance results in a 12 year old pretty bashed machine. / No unaccompanied under 18's permitted after 9pm

11484.info_text: No more DDR, standard bowling alley arcade stuff

11485.info_text: Whilst a lot of arcade machines remain, the majority of the bowling alley building has been a haven for redemption games and ticket machines. Now has StepmaniaX - deluxe cab!!

11487.info_text: Has smallish size arcade with standard games. No ddr but there is a StepmaniaX Deluxe Cabinet.

11490.info_text: Please note that this location is currently under refurbishment. / Most of the arcade games are in a pop up arcade in the ICON outlet, but will return to this location when refurb is complete.

11494.info_text: just the regular type of games for a bowling alley these days, DDR not there.

11497.info_text: Located inside the red dragon centre, it is bowling around the back, arcade round the front on left and right. / You don't have to be bowling to go to arcade. / [ ! ] Paid parking, smx not included / Recently (late July 2024 ish?) the arcade has been fully reshuffled with new machines and such with the deli on the right being replaced by arcade. / Average bowling arcade, 10p machines, redemption games w/ tickets, etc. / Some machines have card readers, there is a £1 machine near entrance on left that also accepts card and cash where you can get coins. / I sent an email to them asking if they could turn up the volume and they actually did so yay / 2nd StepManiaX in Wales!

11498.info_text: Opened 20th July 2026 / Multiple floor "XL" location with bowling, go karts, darts, and arcade.

11501.info_text: Recently opened in 2024, and has all the usual amenities including mini golf.

11502.info_text: As you enter turn left into arcade area. They are all the way at the back by the the back exit.

11505.info_text: **Please note** / Hollywood Bowl Recently updated their Card Reader suppliers to Tigapo So any existing cards No longer functions on the readers. If you have any ask at reception if you can migrate / swap to the new cards and they can carry your data across. Additionally, Other than the 10p pushers none of the other games are coinless meaning you have to use the cards.

11508.info_text: Nice size arcade with the standard type of games, sadly no DDR.

11509.info_text: Average Hollywood Bowl machines. Redemptions, a few racers and shooters dotted in the bowling alley.

11511.info_text: In the Quay area. Opened March 2019 and offers bowling and an arcade.

11513.info_text: Used to be really good for dancegames (SN1 + only PIU PRO cab for miles) but they got rid of them for more redemption a while back. Mario Kart is decent but they have little else in the way of actual video games.

11514.info_text: Bowling alley. Arcade is at the far right end of the building.

11515.info_text: Has large arcade with a few of the usual shooter and race games. Lots of ticket machines, pool tables and air hockey. Cafe and bar.

11517.info_text: Opened in September 2023. Has an arcade with a StepManiax Deluxe Cabinet.

11522.info_text: Bowling alley, the 3rd bowling alley in Birmingham.

11523.info_text: Mostly redemption now and arcade games now.

11524.info_text: A bowling alley located in the Valley Centertainment, / 10 pin bowling, amusement arcade and bar.

11526.info_text: ''16 lanes to bowl along, a designated VIP area, an american themed diner, a relaxing bar and an exciting amusements area''

11528.info_text: Typical bowling alley arcade, sadly most of the focus is on redemption games but there are a handful of actual video games to play. It's all quite modern which is actually pretty great, unless of course you're looking for something retro. Most games, bar the Dancing Stage EuroMIX cab, are kept to a really great condition, prices are generally £1 a go, a couple of the bigger machines being £2. / Crowd wise you can often find a lot of kids but they're harmless. Good area for Streetpassing on your Nintendo 3DS! Since Hollywood Bowl is in a leisure park you have a few other attractions such as Odeon, a multitude of places to eat including Nandos, McDonalds, KFC, Pizza Hut, Coast II Coast, Chiquitos, ASK and a couple others I'm forgetting. There is a club nearby called Chicago's which gets very busy on Thursday nights as that is the student night, however I daresay they'd not waste their time in a sub-par arcade over a nightclub haha. / Website says the place is open from 10:00 "til late", I'm not certain what time that means.

11533.info_text: Recently refurbished & rebranded from AMF Bowling to Hollywood Bowl.

11536.info_text: Has various shooters, racers, luck-based ticket-winning games, no dance machines. Does have some large piano key style game but I don't know what that is

11537.info_text: Currently closed due to COVID-19 / Used to have a various amount of Bamco and raw thrills games and I think some VR game but now is focusing more on ticket redemption.

11538.info_text: Small arcade with a some ticket games and a few racers, not too much of note

11541.info_text: Small but well kept. Typical newer arcade and redemption games

11542.info_text: Bowling alley which is cheap and high priced.

11549.info_text: "As I drove past Merlins to that corner by the Rose and Crown that we all love to see, I noticed the 'Mr B's' arcades had been turned into a 'Jimmy G's' instead. Jimmy Godden has bought both sides of Mr B's, both phase I and II. The larger of the two, phase II, has been completely renovated giving it a more modern look. The roof has been completely torn down and replaced, which must have cost one hell of a lot as I know it to have had an asbestos problem, and could not be touched. I was especially sad to notice the three things phase II offered that no other Leysdown arcade offered had been removed: The Laser quest, 'fun factory' and bumper cars have all been demolished. A new bowling alley has been put in its place however, as well as the bingo being built too. Hope fully with Jimmy owning several other arcades too, he will be able to bring a new lease of life to Leysdown, as I'm sure many people would would agree, it could definitely do with a good renovation. / Jimmy Godden / Jimmy Godden is known as the 'King of the South-Coast', owning various different arcades throughout sea-side towns in the South East of England. He seems to be very unlucky with some of these though, wit...

11591.info_text: Very seasonal seaside village. 3 little arcades, this one now having a nice Supernova. It's a tiny arcade, can't believe they've even gotten this. There's more games than listed, as was going by the few photos I took, and didn't get all of them into the photos / From their website / CONSOLE COLLECTION / See a selection of games consoles from our collection, including original models from Commodore, Atari, Nintendo and Sega. / ARCADE GAMES / Recreate the 1980s arcade experience and compete against your friends and family on original arcade machines including Gauntlet, Street Fighter II, Galaxian and Space Invaders. As well as arcades, they also have consoles with games on a multi-card/other multi-game storage, these include SNES, Mega Drive (Genesis), Playstation 1, and Gamecube. / DDR EuroMix 2, everything works pretty well on it, pads can be a little unresponsive but its usually pretty good, but because of how busy the place is you can't be on it for too long, not good for prolonged plays, but good if you wanna flex for like 10 minutes.

But there is also a StepManiaX DX cabinet on the ground floor. The second floor consists mostly of redemption and pool tables. The third floor has a bowling alley, food, drink and toilets. 11681.info_text: Trampoline centre with arcade machines. Some arcade machines are in the cafe and some are in a separate dedicated area/alcove. Either way, it's not stated as being necessary to sign up for a trampolining session to access the machines. Having said that, at least one ziv contributor was prevented from accessing the arcade area due to not having a booking and was informed by the manager that you need to either have a booking or be accompanying someone with a booking to be allowed to walk to the area where the arcade machines are located. / Also, if you don't have a booking, you can't access the O2 itself before it officially opens at 10am and therefore can't access the arcade machines. For example on Saturdays, Oxygen Freejumping nominally opens at 9am and the O2 officially opens at 10am. So if you arrive between 9 and 10, you can't get to the arcade area unless you have a trampolining booking, as O2 security will prevent you from entering the O2 itself. (After 10am you won't have this problem.) Because of this, listed the opening time as 10am each day rather than what it says on the Oxygen website. / In addition to the listed games, there are a few sweet machines: / *Chupa Chups...

11688.info_text: Must have an Entertainment Hub Pass to gain entry to the arcade as it's directly after reception. this then breaks off into the Swimming pool & Showbar via a small corridor and Boathouse Bar and Resturant.

11689.info_text: This arcade is located inside the entertainment hub. / Note you must be either a) Holiday maker or B) own a caravan / This is because you do require a hub pass to access it.

11690.info_text: Amusement arcade located within the Parkdean resort, recently undergone changes such as the new Next Level gaming area, with newer machines.

11691.info_text: An arcade inside the entertainment complex. Not many games here.

11692.info_text: Arcade in Dawlish Warren. Basically Redemption all the way.

11693.info_text: nice bowling alley with a nice looking cafe overlooking the beach, but standard bowling alley games now

11694.info_text: This is a Leisure Centre now owned by the Southwark Council. / 2 arcade games are hidden near the play area. These machines may be turned off occasionally.

11695.info_text: Holiday park with an arcade that has a very good EM1 cab.

11696.info_text: There is a arcade inside the funfair.

11697.info_text: Dance Dance Revolution SuperNOVA Jap. Unlocked version. Excellent condition. / 3 Songs for £1, set to instant fail. / It's easy to spot when you walk in. Considering how out the way our little town is from the rest of the world doing any song over a 7 footer will have people watching. Good place to play, great staff.

11698.info_text: Located directly across the road from California Cliffs Holiday Park. Family owned arcade. Cafe is independent from the arcade.

11699.info_text: New owners, but haven't visited so can't confirm they still have the machines. I'll delete them until further notice.

11700.info_text: A bar that mostly consists of more modern consoles and multigame arcade cabs containing about 40-1000+ games each. Some contain a LOT of games, while others contain few. / Multigames free of charge / Other require tokens, found on ground floor next to Pump cab. / Downstairs there's a PC lab starting at £4.50 an hour. Booking required.

11701.info_text: Freeplay Arcade in Stoke-on-Trent. / Tickets cost £7.50 and can be bought online or at reception. / When booking you must pick a time slot, the available time slots are as follows: / Saturday - 12:30-17:30 & 18:00-22:30 / Sunday - 12:30-17:30 / The arcade has a variety of retro games, Arcade1up cabinets, retro consoles, PIU Exceed and a weird Guitar Hero cabinet.

11702.info_text: I'm hoping they'll add some more games in the future, but it just looks like mame/ pandora's box cabinets as of now.

11703.info_text: Arcade is downstairs. You have to buy something (can just be a drink) then you are allowed to go downstairs and use the machines; everything is free to use. / In addition to the arcade machines they also have consoles. The following consoles were observed: / Nintendo Switch with Mario Kart 8 Deluxe (in Mario Kart themed alcove) / PlayStation 2 with the following games: / *Black / *Brothers in Arms: Earned in Blood / *Call of Duty 3 / *Driv3r / *Fantastic 4 / *The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King / *The Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers / *Medal of Honor: European Assault / *Mortal Kombat: Deadly Alliance / *Need for Speed Underground / *Pirates of the Caribbean: At World's End / *Pro Evolution Soccer 5 / *Star Wars Battlefront II / Xbox 360 with the following games: / *Assassin's Creed II / *Assassin's Creed III / *Batman: Arkham City / *Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare / *Call of Duty: Ghosts / *Dante's Inferno / *Devil May Cry 4 / *Halo 3 / *Max Payne 3 / *Need for Speed: Hot Pursuit / *Resident Evil 5 / *Skate / They also have a variety of board games including 5 Second Rule, Articulate, Beat the Parents, Connect 4, Draughts, Jumanji, Ludo, Mad Wish, The Million Pound...

11704.info_text: FEATURING DISCO DUCK, 30P!!!!!!!!! / GHAC is £2 for premium song / (July 2025 - No longer has a dancing 'stage'. The 3 euromixes are at the back of the arcade) / Has aircon which is pretty nice when upstairs

11706.info_text: Located in The Galleries Shopping Centre / The original free play area is on the left as you walk in: / Great selection of old Konami rhythm games. all music games are in back area. / Also has a bunch of hacked retro consoles with every game on them. / Tickets are for all-day so you will be given a wristband so you can come and go as you please. Month passes are also available, exclusively by in-person inquiry at front desk. / All games set to freeplay or have credit button. / Increased opening hours during half-terms (opening on Tuesdays and Wednesdays), but exact half-term hours vary. Up-to-date information available on website. / Limited selection of snacks and impressive selection of soft drinks and teas available at front desk, 10% discount for month pass holders. / Prices: / Adult: £15 / Child: £12 / 1 hour: £10 / Month Pass: £37.50 / They’ve recently added a pay-to-play area, accessible through a walkway behind the front desk / Payment is done via a paseli charge machine, with paseli enabled on Konami machines, and readers that convert paseli to coins for all other machines / Most games are less than £1 for standard/premium start / Paseli is priced at: / £5 for 1000P / £1...

11707.info_text: Small bar underground with arcade games / Please somebody update this I saw it in person but did not have time to go in. They have games listed on their website with pictures but it is all unconfirmed.

11708.info_text: Mostly a bar but has a arcade. Contactless payment at the bar.

machine_prices.ddr: £1 / 3 songs on Single. / £1 / 3 songs on Versus. / Double premium is enabled!

11709.info_text: This place has a DDR A cab. / Not really a great venue for DDR, machine doesn't get maintained often anymore. / All games slowly being replaced by knock offs/ticket games.

11711.info_text: Dance Cube has been removed from the location around mid June. / Mostly redemption and coin pushers.They may stay open 30 mins longer if they are busy on the way up to close time. Arcade was bought by Genda so could mean more good stuff actually appearing!

11712.info_text: Owned by Bells Leisue. They've moved all it's games except DDR into the new 'Empire' arcade next door.

11713.info_text: A few arcades onsite. / This location is totally seasonal and therefore is only open between approximately May and October, see website for further details: / [url=http://www.pleasurebeachskegness.com/]Pleasure Beach[/url]

11714.info_text: Pleasure Island has the least amount of video arcade machines here, as half the arcade is made up of 2p/10p/ticket machines. However, this does not mean there are no good games here, as there are several of interest.

11715.info_text: One of three neighbouring arcades on the main pier strip, different owners to the other two. Ran predominantly as a small FEC with bowling/mini golf/ice cream bar components alongside the arcade. / Besides the addition of card payment options and more prize redemption, hasn't changed much in several years.

11716.info_text: Largest arcade here, no music games anymore, mostly redemption and fruit machines, plus some of the typical arcade games

11717.info_text: Previously had a Euromix + a Sega arcade. Now both are gone.

11718.info_text: Amusement arcade with rides and a soft play.

11719.info_text: "Set within 52 acres of enclosed coastal parkland in Lowestoft and just 10 mins from the seaside town of Great Yarmouth, Pleasurewood Hills Family Theme Park has so much to do and explore. Experience a ride on the Marble Madness rollercoaster or jump onboard Wipeout, the tallest, fastest and most extreme roller coaster in the East of England! Get soaked on Timber Falls log flume, enjoy some family fun in the Kiddie Zone or simply relax and enjoy fantastic shows with the Sealions and our Playful Parrots."

11720.info_text: Can easily walk into the compound without anyone checking if you're a resident, just mixing between in between all the families, not sealed off like a prison as some Pontin's are LOL. But not really anything worth going in there for, DDR is gone and is mainly redemption games

11721.info_text: Large arcade and typical holiday park stuff. Not easily accessible for non-residents, but you can pay a charge to visit though. If you go during normal check in time for people staying, they can have the gate open. Not open in winter. As of March the resort is now adults only.

11723.info_text: Only allowed in from 8am to 8pm unless you are staying in the hotel part.

11724.info_text: Restaurant and hotel with play area and a few games for kids.

11727.info_text: Arcade machines inside minigolf centre. / In addition to the arcade machines there are 4 "iPub 2" gambling machines.

11730.info_text: Has been recently renovated, there are multiple arcade cabinets leading to the room with Time Crisis and Mario Kart. DDR MAX 2/Euromix 2 is no longer around. / Arcade can get loud and crowded easily as it is between a bar and the bowling alley.

machine_prices.ddr: £1 / 3 songs STANDARD MODE / £1 / 5 songs NONSTOP MODE / £2 / 3 songs DOUBLE MODE / Machine is labelled as £1 per credit but will not accept modern £1 (accepts other moderns tested to 20p).

11731.info_text: 2 typical UK seaside arcades adjacent to outdoor fair rides and dodgems. Has car park.

11732.info_text: Free to play, no entry fee.

11735.info_text: Mostly 2p machines. Has a casino, over 18 section in the back

11736.info_text: Opened 28th September 2019! Used to be on the first and second floor of Castle Quarter but is now only on the first floor. / RR uses a wristband system - pay on entry and all machines are on free play. £13.50 adults and £10.00 children for entire day. / Left side has the bar as well as both consoles and upright arcade machines lined up by the walls. / - TVs on the wall are set up with Wii U and PS3 among others. The PS3 also has a selection of PS2 games (80+) / - There's a back room that has a line-up of classic consoles (from Atari 2600 to Wii) - ask the staff if you want to play a certain game. There is also a small room with a full dedicated Guitar Hero/Rock Band set up! / Right side is all arcade machines! Majority of cabinets are in very good condition and appear to be maintained often. The front desk also sells merchandise like Pokemon cards, plushes and classic game cartridges/consoles (you don't need to pay for entry to check this area out). / Online score board at https://www.retro-replay.games/highscores

11737.info_text: Cool retro arcade and cafe. No DDR or such, but a better place for a play than the amusements in Newquay. Quite a lot of retro games for a fun play if in the area

11738.info_text: Free play arcade and Bar with a selection of game consoles, retro arcade games, rhythm games, pinball machines and mini golf upstairs. / The arcade has a collection of arcade games from across the decades. Lots of arcade and games have been added over time. / Pricing: / £12.95 for adults (16+) / £10.95 for under 16's without an adult. / £8.95 for under 16's with an adult. / Once you get your wristband, you have access to the arcade for the whole day and can leave and enter as many times as you want. / Mini golf is included with the wristband which can be found upstairs (stairs are to the left before you enter the main arcade area.) / All games are set to Freeplay and can be started by pressing the start button, some games will have a button to insert credits, which is located on the coin door on most machines. / There is a community Discord server for this arcade which can also be used for reporting machine faults. [https://discord.gg/fVjmrYMrTM] / The arcade has extended opening hours on school holidays, following Barnsley term times, the extended opening hours are usually 11:00-20:00 on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday. On friday they open earlier at 11:00 and close at 22:00. O...

11739.info_text: Monday - Wednesday: 12:00PM – 10:00PM / Thursday - Saturday : 12:00PM – Midnight / Sunday: 12:00PM - 10:00PM

11742.info_text: Quite large, 2 floor arcade. A lot of redemption, but also your main big cabs. Now has two DDRs!!!! (where did the DS fusion cab go)

11743.info_text: Bowling alley in New Brighton with an arcade.

11744.info_text: Very old fashioned and cheap feeling bowling alley, complete with screaming children running everywhere and making a mess. Very strange and outdated place.

machine_prices.ddr: £1- 1 or 2 players / £2- Doubles / 3 songs per Credit

11745.info_text: Basically, a caravan park, but with an arcade. / DDR A is here inside.

11746.info_text: Supernova gone 31/07/18 :( / Lots of new redemption games in place / Caravan holiday park...but arcade is at the front, before the barriers for residents and car parking in front, and doesn't seem to be bothered if non-residents go. Very large arcade with all sorts of arcade games and ticket games. Season only opening though.

11748.info_text: As of 15/02/2025 / Neat little indie bowling alley with pool tables and a passable selection of arcade games. Visited on a late friday afternoon and it was pretty lively (and mobbed with children). Has "leisure center inside a RAF base" vibes. Bus routes are pretty inconvenient, requiring a short walk to and from the nearest bus stop. / The Highlands of Scotland are hardly a mecca for arcade games, and I can't imagine tourists wanting to give it a look (since it's so far away from the city center, and the selection is so sparse). Still, if you're local, it's nice to know there's a few rail shooters and driving cabinets to play.

11749.info_text: Arcade is beyond the paid entry gate. It costs £1 to gain access to the arcade, you do not have to bowl to access it.

11751.info_text: All the arcade machines are gone now, all they have left are 2 basketball machines

11752.info_text: A few games here, but all you see is redemption.

11754.info_text: Sand Le Mere Holiday Village Entertainment Venue, You Can Only Access This If You Are Staying at the Caravans.

11755.info_text: UPDATE 09/2015: Visited today, there are currently two DDR machines, a Euromix 2 cabinet running the original Euromix, and a Supernova. While the Euromix is Fine, the Supernova is an Issue (see game info for more) Also for sake of machine locations: I will specify 3 sections: / Section 1: The front half of the pier. Open all year round. Has a indoor minigolf which takes up the majority of the space in this section. / Section 2: The back half of the pier. Has the majority of the games, DDR Included. Closed in the week during low season (October-March) / Section 3: A little shack behind the main pier with a few additional games. / Very nice place, however it is slightly more special to me as I've been going since I was young for holidays, and now I live on the Island. There are toilets available on site as you go in (either side of the entrance) Food and drink is also available to purchase on site as well.

11756.info_text: Small arcade conjoined to pub. Small "family arcade" with a few 2p pushers. Had a decent'ish Extreme, but wasn't there on visit today :(

11760.info_text: Not the best arcade in my opinion.

11761.info_text: An arcade mantained by Park Holidays Uk and is 1 of 3 in clacton.

11762.info_text: Arcade attached to Wendy's in separate room. / Has other games such as air hockey, basket ball hoops and has a soft play area

11765.info_text: An arcade located inside the Shell Island Campsite as part of the facilities. Located near the bar

11766.info_text: Arcade in treasure island. Lots of ticket redemption machines and an 18+ area with slots. DDR cabinet is hidden at the back with the rail shooters.

11767.info_text: Rustic seaside amusement, good playing Euromix2 though! Reckon quite seasonal hours, but we were there on a Weds in Feb, and was open at least. / Update 05/11/2022 / As far as I know the Euromix 2 isn't there anymore, however it may have just being repaired or in storage.

11768.info_text: A basic arcade which consists of mostly redemption machines and not much else

11770.info_text: An arcade that leads onto the very long Southport Pier [Of which the pier is closed currently] / The arcade contains a mixture of Silcock's other arcades including 2p machines, redemptions and bandits. However it does contain a small collection of, what appear to be, poorly maintained video games

11771.info_text: Appeared to be a mixture of Bandits and possibly redemption (Didnt enter), also possibly has pool/bowling in the back / [Unknown opening times but i would assume something around 10:00 -> 22:00]

11772.info_text: A very basic arcade with mostly 2p machines and some bandits / [Unknown opening times but i would assume something around 10:00 -> 22:00]

11775.info_text: Big arcade, lots of games, but they've sadly been maintaining their DDR less and less over the years. The Supernova is at Fantasy Island, in the Pyramid, don't know where the EM2 has gone

11776.info_text: A fair arcade with a few games.

11782.info_text: Is now open for business! / As far as actual arcade games though, it's mostly ticket games around here.

11783.info_text: As of 28/08/2018 the front arcade is open again. PIU working fine too / Open late through high season, usually until 6pm off season. Huge arcade, with the usual mix of games and fruit machines. / 4 pinball near back entrance

11785.info_text: Over the past few years this pier's arcade section has had a few renovations with a completely new look, thus getting rid of a few old arcade machines, including Dancing Stage Euromix.

11786.info_text: Medium sized barcade over two floors. Mixture of consoles and arcade machines. / Update 16/02/25 / Honestly avoid at all costs. I haven't been to a place like this with such miserable staff before. Not only that most of their games are off, broken or just in general really neglected. Don't waste your time or money and instead visit somewhere like NQ64 in Newcastle.

11788.info_text: Decently sized arcade. Lots of kids games and ticket machines, but some well priced shooters in between.

11789.info_text: Manned by Park Holidays UK and one of the 3 holiday parks in clacton.

11790.info_text: Bowling alley and general game place (i.e. shuffleboard, darts and ice free curling) that has a small arcade section. Pay per game - most games have a card reader directly on them

11791.info_text: Venue is 100% cashless. Pricing is as follows. / £10.00 for 100 Credits / £20.00 for 250 Credits / £30.00 for 400 Credits / £50.00 for 700 Credits / credits can now be split between cards, up to 6 cards I believe.

11793.info_text: Large, nicely updated arcade in general. Decent and playable Euromix2 at the mo. All the main Raw Thrills etc cabs and redemption

11794.info_text: Mainly redemption and such / This is owned by the same people as Treasure Island, not sure if tickets work for both here and there but i assume so

11795.info_text: Typical bowling alley, machine gets moderate use.

11798.info_text: Caravan park arcade open to non-res. Very small arcade and very seasonal.

11800.info_text: Small arcade, mostly redemption - unsurprisingly I suppose / Despite this location not having any BEMANI titles at present, this arcade has one of the very few synced Guitar Hero cabinets.

11804.info_text: First opened in 2021. Home of Sega Prize Zone, featuring mostly redemption games and some driving games.

11805.info_text: Decently large arcade connected to a bowling Alley. Has a soft play for kids as well as interactive dartboards. / Email: hull@superbowluk.co.uk / Open 9am until Midnight, Monday to Sunday, during school holidays. / Games missing from website: / Cocobowl / Yellow Submarine 2

11806.info_text: No DDR, a handful of typical games and redemption, laser tag thing, kids soft play area, food and drink

11807.info_text: The Usual Sega Prize Zone stuff.

11808.info_text: Bowling alley with primarily redemption arcade machines in it. Contains some other activities including bowling, laser tag, etc.

11809.info_text: Euromix 2 lives here. Fairly good condition with raised pads. Can often get pad misses however. Used to be on 5 songs for £1 but this has been reduced to 3.

11811.info_text: Is a hotel and pub with a very small games room in the back, behind the beer garden. Previously had DDR but now gone, games room in the back has some general coin pushers and such

11814.info_text: Bowling prices are online or in centre. / Pool Tables are only £1.50 per play.

11818.info_text: Your typical arcade games, shoot 'em ups and racing, Pac Man smash, pool tables, table tennis and redemption. From October 2019 this place is updated and now have a VR Zone.

11819.info_text: Recently opened in Chester with the usual arcade games and redemption.

Don't bother, unless you're going bowling there with friends or family.

11825.info_text: All music games have been removed and replaced with a ping-pong table (yes, really). / All the games that remain are shitty Raw Thrills cabs. / I don't know how exactly Tenpin Derby could get worse, but...well...it just did. / (No Dance Machines) - January 2017

11827.info_text: The location has recently undergone a refurbishment, and they now offer a Storm VR simulator.

11829.info_text: Bowling Alley and Lazer quest venue. / The arcade used to be a lot better and used to have games such as DDR SuperNOVA, Guitar Hero Arcade and Mario Kart. It’s a shell of it’s former self.

11831.info_text: Arcade section of this location freely accessible; No reservation/lane required in order to play the arcade machines.

11834.info_text: This Tenpin only has 10 bowling lanes, laser tag, and an arcade. Despite this, there's only a few redemption games and no racing arcade games.

11836.info_text: This was formerly Harlow Bowl, but is now under new ownership by Tenpin.

11837.info_text: Generic Tenpin Arcade. Recently refurbished. Used to have Dancing Stage Euromix 2 then Pump It Up : Infinity both Now gone sadly .

11841.info_text: This location in Manchester has late opening hours but has also a PIU Infinity. / They also have many arcade games and air hockey, as well as your usuals. / Note that this place no longer allows under 21s after 9pm, so be sure to have some form of ID as the restrictions only last until closing time.

11843.info_text: Arcade is at the front of the bowling on the left and right, your fine to go in even if not bowling. / Pool tables available around the back right, either for half hour, hour or just one round / A lot of raw thrills cabs, hockey table games, general redemption games and such, they shuffle around sometimes.

11845.info_text: HOW / HOW DID IT GET WORSE / THE BAR WAS SET SO LOW IT WAS WELDED TO THE FUCKING FLOOR AND THEY STILL FOUND A WAY TO FLOP UNDER IT / (Fusion finally put out of its misery as of 2022. Place received a £500k revamp and they have perhaps wisely downsized + moved the arcade area as a result)

11849.info_text: Opened in 2024 with all the usual amenities.

11850.info_text: Looking for fun things to do in Southampton? / Tenpin Southampton has you covered with bowling, karaoke, interactive darts, and more under one roof. Sing your heart out in our private karaoke rooms, aim for victory in the laser tag arena, or test your skills in one of our thrilling escape rooms by Houdini’s. / Kids can enjoy our vibrant soft play area, while groups will love the challenge of Prison Putt—our unique indoor golf experience. We also have the best kid's bowling parties in town, let us take all the stress out of the day and book with us. It doesn't stop there though, we also have karaoke, laser tag, and Prison Putt parties for kids and adults alike. / With a stylish bar, tasty food, arcade games, pool, and table tennis, it’s the perfect spot for family fun, parties, or nights out in Southampton.

11851.info_text: Formerly Premier Bowl, but has now rebranded as Tenpin.

11858.info_text: Tenpin bowling alley with arcade games

11859.info_text: The usual redemption and arcade fare.
